Cloche avant lente

The engine telegraph order for slow speed ahead, typically used during precise manoeuvring, docking, or when entering confined waters.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Cloche avant lente?

In this glossary, Cloche avant lente refers to: The engine telegraph order for slow speed ahead, typically used during precise manoeuvring, docking, or when entering confined waters.

How is Cloche avant lente used in maritime?

In maritime communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Donnez la cloche avant lente lorsque le navire quitte le quai et maintenez la vitesse pour une manœuvre précise dans la zone restreinte."

Why does Cloche avant lente matter in maritime?

Cloche avant lente matters because it supports clear communication in Nav contexts for Deck Officers, Engine Officers, and Masters. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as STCW, Marlins Test, ISF Watchkeeper, and GMDSS.

Who uses Cloche avant lente?

Cloche avant lente is mainly used by Deck Officers, Engine Officers, and Masters.

What category does Cloche avant lente belong to?

In this glossary, Cloche avant lente is grouped under Nav. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from IMO SMCP, STCW Convention, SOLAS, COLREG and published by Protermify Maritime as a static maritime reference page.

Definition

The engine telegraph order for slow speed ahead, typically used during precise manoeuvring, docking, or when entering confined waters.

Operational example

Give slow ahead bell when vessel is clear of berth and maintain speed for precise manoeuvring in restricted area.

Localized term

Cloche avant lente

Localized example

Donnez la cloche avant lente lorsque le navire quitte le quai et maintenez la vitesse pour une manœuvre précise dans la zone restreinte.
